hlido_opinion.headline: An Apache-2.0 MCP hub/proxy that aggregates servers, memory and tools — well-documented, lightly adopted, and a touch stale at review time.
hlido_opinion.body: plugged.in MCP Proxy is an aggregation layer: it sits in front of multiple MCP servers and presents them as one hub, adding knowledge, memory and tooling on top. On the repository signals it reads as a serious project — Apache-2.0 licensed, a 31K-char README, two CI workflows, and MCP server markers so a client can wire it up. Where it is thinner is momentum and adoption: 132 stars is modest for infrastructure that wants to be a central hub, and the last push was ~67 days before review, so it is maintained but not fast-moving. For teams evaluating an MCP aggregation layer it is a credible, permissively-licensed option to trial; the register scores its repository health, not the runtime reliability of the proxy under load, which was not tested here.

tier_rationale: STEADY (82), the repo-surface ceiling: reachable, Apache-2.0, a thorough 31K-char README, two CI workflows, MCP server markers, and commits within the year. Not VITAL because proxy runtime behavior (routing correctness, latency, failure handling under real MCP traffic) needs hands-on testing the repo signals cannot supply; adoption (132 stars) and a ~67-day-stale tip also temper the ceiling.
what_it_does_well: Thorough README (31K chars) documenting install and usage
Two CI workflows present — some automated quality gating
MCP server markers make client integration straightforward
Clear, focused purpose: proxy + knowledge + memory + tools in one hub
what_it_fails_at: No tagged releases — versioning/upgrade story is informal
Last push ~67 days before review — maintained but not actively iterating
Runtime proxy behavior under real MCP load was not tested
best_for: Teams wanting to aggregate several MCP servers behind one endpoint
Users who need an Apache-2.0-licensed MCP hub they can self-host
Setups that also want memory/knowledge layered onto the proxy
not_recommended_for: Production deployments needing a formally released, versioned artifact
Buyers who require a proven-at-scale, supported proxy

compared_to.verdict_diff: Both are MCP aggregation layers. mcp-gateway (PMCP) ships tagged releases (v1.19.3) and a PyPI package with heavier CI; pluggedin-mcp-proxy leans on a richer hub feature set (knowledge/memory) but has no releases. Choose mcp-gateway for a versioned, packaged gateway; choose pluggedin for the broader hub features.
Both are MCP-surface projects in the register; wisepanel is a single MCP server, pluggedin is a proxy that fronts many. Pick pluggedin when the problem is fan-in across multiple servers.
